children: The ₹2,100 crore Initial Public Offer (IPO) of Elevate Campuses Ltd. opens for subscription on Wednesday, September 23. The complete fresh issue of shares will be open for subscription until Friday, September 25.
Elevate Campuses has priced the IPO between ₹343 to ₹362 per share, which, at the upper end of the price band, will give the company a market capitalization of ₹6,100 crore.

One lot will comprise of 41 shares and small retail investors will have to make a minimum investment of ₹14,842 to bid for one lot and then in multiples of 41 shares thereafter. Only 10% of the issue is reserved for retail investors.
75% of the IPO is reserved for Qualified Institutional Bidders (QIBs), while the other 15% is reserved for non-institutional investors (NIIs).
A completely promoter-held company, the promoter stake in Elevate Campuses after the IPO will fall to 65.58% from 100% currently.
What Does Elevate Campuses Do?

Owned by Hillhouse Investment, Singapore, Elevate Campuses owns and manages student housing for colleges and universities and owns K-12 school buildings that it leases out. It must be noted that the company is an education infrastructure provider and not an educator itself.

The company owns hostels, PGs on or near the university campuses such as Manipal, Jindal Global, Shoolini among others. Among the total number of beds they have, 20,368 are fully owned, while 55,487 are run under management contracts for the institution, thereby earning them rent / fees for dining, laundry, gym, and other campus services.
A K-12 entity is an educational institution that provides schooling from Kindergarten till the 12th grade.
How Will Elevate Campuses Use IPO Proceeds?
Nearly 50% of the ₹2,100 crore that it plans on raising will be used to acquire 16 K-12 entities and campuses from the promoter group and connected entities.
Another ₹750 crore will be used to repay / pre-pay borrowings, while the rest will be used for unidentified inorganic growth and general corporate purposes.
How Do The Elevate Campuses Financials Stack Up?
During financial year 2026, Elevate Campuses reported a 32.2% year-on-year growth in its topline to ₹806.9 crore from ₹610.5 crore.
Its EBITDA margin expanded sharply from 66.5% in financial year 2025 to 85.9%, while profitability tripled to ₹207 crore from ₹68.1 crore in financial year 2025.
What Are The Risks To The Elevate Campuses IPO?
As highlighted earlier and in the RHP, 52.38% of the issue proceeds will be used to fund a promoter-group acquisition (K-12 assets).

Over the past three financial years and including the current financial year, there have been instances of delayed payments by K-12 Operators, with delays ranging from one to six months in certain cases.
The owned bed occupancy has also declined from 99.92% in financial year 2024 to 99.47% in financial year 2025 and then to 89.37% in financial year 2026.
Should You Subscribe To The Elevate Campuses IPO?

According to SBI Securities, growth will be driven by the addition of 2,128 beds at IIT Madras and UPES Dehradun combined going forward, and by scaling of the asset-light managed portfolio and consolidation of the 16 domestic K-12 assets.
Even as the proposed ₹750 crore earmarked to repay debt, SBI Securities believes that debt levels will remain elevated going forward as well.
Therefore, SBI Securities has a "neutral" rating on Elevate Campuses and will like to track the performance of the company for a few quarters after listing.
What Is The Elevate Campuses IPO GMP Indicating?
Ahead of the IPO opening, Elevate Campuses shares in the unlisted market commanded a premium of ₹16 per share.
It must be noted that these Grey Market Premium (GMP) rates are speculative in nature and the actual rates can differ from what the GMP rates are indicating.

title: Elevate Campuses IPO opens for subscription today: Should you bid for the ₹2,100 crore issue?
